question.problem: By the multiplicative property of congruences, $77\cdot 82≡$
question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}77 & ≡12\cdot 6+5\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡12\cdot 0+5\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡5\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ 82 & ≡13\cdot 6+4\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡13\cdot 0+4\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡4\, & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}77\cdot 82 & ≡5\cdot 4\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡20\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡3\cdot 6+2\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡3\cdot 0+2\, & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
77\cdot 82≡2\,(\text{mod}\,6).
$$
